## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).

Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.

15	- .goreleaser.yaml building cmd/harnaas for darwin/linux/windows on amd64/arm64 with CGO disabled, stamping Version and Commit into cmd/harnaas/cli/versioninfo via ldflags
16	- .github/workflows/ci.yml with SHA-pinned actions and lint, licenses, test and test-windows jobs behind a single 'ci' aggregator job intended as the required status check
17	- .allowed-licenses SPDX allowlist plus a go-licenses gate wired as the lint:licenses task
18	- CLAUDE.md recording the imported architecture rules (flat cli package, no persistent flags, entrypoint-owns-errors, exit-code taxonomy, signal re-raise, context-carried project root, strict-vs-lenient decoding, logging privacy, atomic writes) with AGENTS.md pointing at it

21	- The reference entire.io CLI is checked out at C:\Users\brasp\Documents\GitHub\cli and its mise.toml, .golangci.yaml, mise-tasks/lint/* and .github/workflows are directly adaptable — future iterations should read from it rather than inventing conventions.
22	- A GitHub Actions aggregator job can only 'needs' jobs within its own workflow file, so task 1.7's 'workflows for test and lint plus a single aggregator job' was implemented as one ci.yml containing all jobs.
23	- Task 1.1 asks for directories that git cannot track empty; cmd/harnaas needs a buildable main.go (placeholder here, replaced by task 2.2) and internal/ was given a README recording the import-cycle-only extraction rule.
24	- mise on Windows requires 'mise trust' before any task runs, and it happily executes the /bin/sh mise-tasks scripts via git-bash — but the CI windows job deliberately uses plain 'go test ./...' instead.
25	- mise-tasks/lint/gomod fails on a brand-new repo because 'git status --porcelain go.mod' reports the untracked file; it only passes once go.mod is committed.
26	- Verification tooling not installed locally can be run one-off via 'mise x <tool> -- <cmd>' — used for 'goreleaser check' and yq to validate .goreleaser.yaml and ci.yml without adding them to mise.toml.

29	
30	**Summary:** Completed Section 2 of the add-harnaas-foundation change — the process entrypoint, two-stage signal handling, error-rendering contract and exit-code taxonomy — plus the versioninfo package it depends on, taking the change from 9/74 to 17/74 tasks with lint, format and tests all clean.
31	
32	**Changes:**
33	- internal/procsignal records the signal that initiated shutdown in an atomic.Value, giving the entrypoint a single source of truth for whether a context.Canceled was signal-driven and by which signal, so SIGTERM exits 143 rather than impersonating an interrupt's 130
34	- cmd/harnaas/cli/versioninfo exposes ldflags-stamped Version/Commit with a pure resolve core: an explicit stamp beats Go's embedded build info, which beats the dev placeholder; goreleaser's existing -X stamps now target a package that exists
35	- cmd/harnaas/cli/errors.go adds AlreadyPrintedError with Unwrap and the NewAlreadyPrintedError constructor, so a command that printed a friendly explanation can suppress the entrypoint's restatement without hiding the cause from errors.Is/errors.As
36	- cmd/harnaas/cli/root.go builds the root command with cobra's error and usage printing silenced, no persistent flags, a version template carrying the commit, and Args: cobra.NoArgs so an unrecognized verb is reported as an unknown command even before subcommands exist
37	- cmd/harnaas/main.go replaces the placeholder with the full process contract: versioninfo.Load, a cancellable root context, a two-stage signal handler (first cancels and prints the force-quit notice, second forces exit), dieFromSignal re-raising the original signal with a 128+signum fallback, and the error switch routing already-printed / unknown-command-or-flag / positional-arg / plain errors
38	- The exit-code taxonomy is stated as documented constants in main.go — 0 success, 1 runtime failure, 2 reserved for lint findings with the negative rule that no other command may return it — and a test asserts no entrypoint error path can produce 2
39	- Test coverage for section 2: a re-executed-child test proving the process is killed by the signal rather than exiting normally (skipped on Windows), the 128+signum mapping including a non-numeric signal, terminatingSignal's gate on a recorded signal, every branch of the error switch driven by both synthetic and real cobra errors, and proof cobra prints neither error nor usage itself
40	- cobra v1.10.2 and testify v1.11.1 added to go.mod, with the go-licenses gate confirming every new transitive dependency's license is on the allowlist
41	
42	**Learnings:**
43	- Task ordering in tasks.md is not a strict dependency order: task 2.2 ("load version info") requires task 4.1's versioninfo package and a root command from section 3, so 4.1 was pulled forward. Section 3.1 was left unchecked deliberately — the root command exists but has no help groups or subcommand attachments yet.
44	- Cobra's legacyArgs makes a root command with no subcommands accept arbitrary positional args, so `harnaas bogus` silently printed help and exited 0. Setting `Args: cobra.NoArgs` on the root produces cobra's own `unknown command "bogus" for "harnaas"` message, which the entrypoint's classifier already matches, and stays correct once subcommands land.
45	- mise tasks cannot be launched from the PowerShell tool on this machine ("program not found" — mise shells out to `sh`); they must be run through the Bash tool. Running golangci-lint directly via `mise x -- golangci-lint run` is the way to see lint results, because a failing sibling task in the `lint` fan-out kills the whole group before lint:go reports.
46	- The `testifylint` linter with enable-all requires `require.*` rather than `assert.*` for every error assertion (ErrorIs/ErrorAs), which is the only lint class the new code tripped.

Renaming the method to `String()` is the better fix than renaming the type: a single violation is never what a command returns, so it should not satisfy `error` at all, and the linter's complaint turned out to be pointing at a real design question.
214	- `unparam` with check-exported fires on an unexported constructor whose field parameter always receives the same value, which will happen to every helper written ahead of the call sites that will vary it. Naming the narrow case (assetSourceViolation) rather than suppressing the linter keeps the diff honest — sections 7.5–7.7 will add the sibling constructors when they add the fields.
215	- `path.Clean` treats a backslash as an ordinary character, so a keyed path like `acme:skills\review` passes every containment check and produces a ref naming a file that exists on Windows and not on Linux. The grammar has to reject backslashes explicitly, ahead of cleaning; the absolute-path check has to run first so `C:\...` and `\\share\...` get the message about absolute paths instead.
216	- `path.Ext` treats a leading dot as the whole extension, so stripping unconditionally turns `.editorconfig` into an empty id. Only a non-empty remainder can replace the leaf.
217	- testifylint's useless-assert rejects `assert.Equal(t, f(), f())`, which is the obvious way to write 'this function returns a stable list'. Comparing both calls against a literal expected slice is what the linter wants and is a stronger assertion anyway, because it pins the order rather than only its stability.
218	- The Bash tool's working directory persists between calls, so a `cd` into a package directory silently rescopes a later `go test ./...` or `golangci-lint run ./...` to that package — which reports 0 issues and looks like a pass. Prefix repo-wide verification with an explicit cd to the repository root.
219	
220	### Iteration 10
221	
222	**Summary:** Added the manifest interpretation layer's defaulting half — the object override form, target defaulting and scope defaulting (Section 7, tasks 7.5–7.7) — taking the add-harnaas-foundation change from 44/74 to 47/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.
223	
224	**Changes:**
225	- cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest/asset.go declares Scope (project/user) and Asset — one manifest entry with every question answered, where each field an entry may leave undeclared has already been inferred from its path or defaulted from the document, so a later phase cannot treat a declared `type` differently from an implied one
226	- ResolveType and ResolveID implement the object form's suppression rule one field at a time: a declared type is deliberately not checked against the path it overrides, because the object form exists precisely for a source whose layout does not follow the convention, and comparing them would refuse the case it was added for; a type outside harnaas's own vocabulary is still rejected, listing the five
227	- ResolveTargets returns the entry's own `targets` when declared and the manifest's `harnesses` otherwise, and returns a list of violations rather than one because `targets` is itself a list — each unrecognized name attributed to its own position (`assets[3].targets[0]`) so the aggregate orders identically on every run
228	- The nil-versus-empty Targets distinction decoding preserved is spent in ResolveTargets: an entry that declares nothing where the manifest declares no harnesses, and an entry that declares an empty list, both have nowhere to install but get different messages because they need different edits
229	- CheckHarnesses validates the document's own `harnesses` list once, at DocumentIndex with field `harnesses[1]`, so a misspelling there is one message rather than one per asset that inherited it; an empty list is deliberately not reported at document level, because it is only a problem for an asset that would have inherited it
230	- ResolveScope defaults to `project`, refuses a scope harnaas does not define, refuses `user` on an instruction pointing at `rule` as the type for that intent, and refuses `user` for any target the roster records no per-user location for — naming every offending target in one sentence and never falling back to project scope
231	- resolveScope takes the roster query as a parameter so the no-per-user-location refusal has a test today, when every harness on the roster has one; a target the roster does not know is skipped rather than reported twice, because the field that declared it already reported it
232	- violation.go generalizes assetSourceViolation into assetViolation(index, field, …), giving every per-field asset diagnostic the same `assets[N].<field>` spelling that the deterministic ordering in 7.9 sorts on
233	- Test coverage across an external file for the exported surface and an internal file for the roster seam: declared-beats-inferred in both directions, an unknown type, inherited and narrowed targets, both empty-effective-list cases, two unrecognized targets producing two positioned violations, the document-level harness list, the scope default in both entry forms, an undefined scope, user-on-an-instruction, and the four per-user-location branches including the plural sentence
234	- CLAUDE.md records the two load-bearing decisions — a default is inherited and checked once, and a wrong scope is refused rather than degraded — together with why the refusal needs a seam to be testable before the first harness without a per-user location is added
235	
236	**Learnings:**
237	- Validating an inherited default per asset would multiply one mistake by the number of entries that inherited it, so the manifest's `harnesses` list is checked once at DocumentIndex and ResolveTargets checks only what the entry itself declared. The consequence is that an inherited unrecognized name still reaches Asset.Targets — which is safe only because a document with any violation is never handed to a later phase, and that is now a load-bearing invariant rather than a convenience.
238	- Section 7.7's core rule is untestable against the real roster: claude-code is the only entry and it has PerUserLocation true, so there is no target for which `user` scope can be refused. Passing harness.HasPerUserLocation as a parameter to an unexported resolveScope — the same seam pattern jsonutil.writeFileAtomic already uses for its flush step — is what keeps the rule from rotting until the first harness that lacks a per-user location is added.
239	- A per-field violation helper has to produce a field name that sorts deterministically, which is why an unrecognized target is spelled `assets[3].targets[0]` rather than sharing one `assets[3].targets` field with its siblings. Lexical rather than numeric ordering of the bracketed index is a known and accepted consequence — 7.9 specifies ordering by index then field, and lexical field order is exactly that.
240	- gocritic's unlambda fires on a test closure that only forwards to the function it wraps, so a seam test wanting to pass the real implementation must pass the function value directly rather than wrapping it for readability; the explanatory comment has to move above the call site.
241	- Two test files for one source file is already the established convention here (jsonutil splits json_test.go external from write_test.go internal), so an exported-surface test in package manifest_test plus an internal test for the seam needs no justification beyond naming the internal one asset_internal_test.go.
242	- Task 7.8's aggregate is now the only thing standing between these resolvers and a usable interpretation entry point: every piece it needs (ParseSource, ParseAssetRef, CheckSourceKey, ResolveType, ResolveID, ResolveTargets, CheckHarnesses, ResolveScope) exists and returns Violations carrying index and field, so 7.8 is assembly plus the two cross-entry rules (duplicate ids within a type, unsafe id segments) rather than new interpretation.
243	
244	### Iteration 11
245	
246	**Summary:** Added the manifest interpretation entry point — the accumulating aggregate, cross-entry id rules and deterministic ordering (Section 7, tasks 7.8–7.10) — completing Section 7 and taking the add-harnaas-foundation change from 47/74 to 50/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.
247	
248	**Changes:**
249	- cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest/interpret.go adds Interpret(doc), the second layer's whole entry point: it parses every `sources` value, checks the document's harness list once, interprets every asset entry, and returns an *Interpretation carrying the document, the parsed sources and the resolved assets — or nothing at all, which is how 'a document with any violation is never handed to a later phase' is enforced rather than merely stated, since Interpret is the only route to an Asset
250	- interpretEntry accumulates within an entry instead of returning at its first problem, but declines to ask a question whose answer would have to be invented: where the source string did not parse there is no path to infer a type or an id from, so inference is skipped unless the entry declared the field itself, while targets and every declared field are still checked
251	- A source key whose value is malformed is registered as declared, so the asset referencing it is not blamed for a mistake it did not make — the violation stays on `sources.<key>` where the edit is
252	- CheckID rejects an id that is not a single safe path segment — any slash or backslash, `.` and `..` — because an id names a file the installer creates inside a harness's directory; an empty id passes, because whatever left the entry without one has already said so
253	- checkDuplicateIDs asks the one question no single entry can answer about itself, last and only over entries with nothing else wrong: uniqueness is per type rather than per manifest, and a collision is attributed to the later entry naming the earlier one so it is one violation rather than two
254	- manifest.ValidationError in errors.go is the aggregate: file, problem count in the singular or plural, then every violation in the problem-then-fix shape, with Violations exposed already ordered so a caller rendering them itself sees what the message would have shown
255	- sortViolations orders by asset index then field, putting document-level problems first through DocumentIndex being negative, so two runs over one manifest produce byte-identical output despite `sources` decoding into a map
256	- interpret_test.go adds the documented example manifest as a fixture that decodes strictly and interprets clean with every field asserted, a manifest with six independent violations asserting the exact reported order, a twenty-run determinism check over a four-key sources block, both halves of the per-type uniqueness rule, a table over every accepted and rejected id spelling, the aggregate's own rendering in both the singular and plural, and a re-assertion that no remedy offers a command
257	- CLAUDE.md records the three new load-bearing decisions — Interpret as the only route to an Asset, the refusal to invent a problem the author never wrote, and per-type uniqueness attributed to the later entry — and the manifest package doc now names Load and Interpret as the whole of each layer
258	- Tasks 7.8, 7.9 and 7.10 checked off, completing Section 7
259	
260	**Learnings:**
261	- Task 7.10's table-driven tests over 'every grammar, inference and validation rule' were already delivered piecewise by iterations 9 and 10 (source_test.go, assetref_test.go, asset_test.go); only its two document-level fixtures — the documented example loading clean, and a manifest reporting several violations at once — were outstanding, so the task closes with the 7.8 work rather than needing a pass of its own.
262	- The 'never handed to a later phase' rule is only enforceable if the interpreted type is unreachable without the check. Returning ([]Asset, error) and letting callers ignore the error would leave the rule as documentation; returning a single *Interpretation that is nil on any violation makes it structural, and is why the type exists at all rather than Interpret returning the pieces separately.
263	- A malformed `sources` value would otherwise produce two violations for one mistake — the bad value, and every asset 'referencing an undeclared key'. Registering the key with a zero Source when its value fails to parse keeps CheckSourceKey satisfied, because the key genuinely is declared; only its value is not.
264	- Skipping type and id inference when the source string failed to parse is what stops one bad asset string from producing three violations, since InferType and InferID would both run against an empty path. The guard is `refParsed || entry.<field> != ""`, which keeps a declared field checked even when the path it would have overridden is unusable.
265	- Every violation constructor already carried its index and field as data from iterations 9 and 10, so 7.9's determinism requirement was one slices.SortStableFunc over (Index, Field) with no changes to any producer — the design decision that made this cheap was made two iterations before it paid off.
266	- Sections 8 (init) and 9 (guardrail tests) are now the only implementation work left, and neither depends on Interpret: init writes a scaffold and never reads assets, so the interpretation layer has no caller in this change and will first be exercised by add-harnaas-install.
267	
268	### Iteration 12
269	
270	**Summary:** Added the `harnaas init` command end to end — detection, selection, confirmation, the scaffold and its single-file guarantee (Section 8, tasks 8.1–8.11) — taking the add-harnaas-foundation change from 50/74 to 61/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.
271	
272	**Changes:**
273	- cmd/harnaas/cli/init.go adds `harnaas init` with --force, -y/--yes and a repeatable --harness registered locally on the command, and a RunE whose step order is the contract: everything that can refuse — an unrecognized harness name, a manifest already at the root — happens before the prompt and before anything is written, so no question is asked whose answer cannot change the outcome
274	- The scaffold is its own type rather than manifest.Document, because Document is what decoding produces and this is the file: version 1, the selected harnesses, and `sources`/`assets` written empty rather than omitted so an author opening the file sees where their content goes; it is encoded through jsonutil and written atomically, so a forced run either replaces the previous manifest in full or leaves it intact with no staging file behind
275	- cmd/harnaas/cli/init_select.go resolves the `harnesses` list: --harness replaces detection entirely rather than merging with it, duplicate names are written once, an unrecognized one returns the roster's own finished diagnostic, and detection stats the roster's evidence paths in roster order while creating nothing
276	- detectHarnesses takes the roster as a parameter so the "every detected harness appears, deterministically ordered" rule has a test today, when claude-code is the only entry — the same seam pattern resolveScope uses for the per-user-location refusal
277	- Confirmation goes through uiform on stderr, and is skipped automatically with --yes or wherever prompting is impossible, so the whole command is completable with no terminal; a cancelled prompt writes nothing and returns an error wrapping uiform.ErrCancelled, while a decline writes nothing and exits 0 — both write nothing, and only the cancelled run left the question unanswered
278	- Success prints the created path and `harnaas install` as the next command on stdout, and describes the remaining setup — .harnaas/, the harness directories, the ignore-file entries — as guidance naming the command that performs it, with no flag that makes init perform any of it
279	- init is attached to the root under the setup group, with the commented install and lint attachments moved below it because a group's header renders where its first command was attached
280	- cmd/harnaas/cli/init_test.go covers section 8 end to end: the scaffold decoding and interpreting clean through the real loader, the written file asserted line for line, detection with one and (through the roster seam) several harnesses, the fallback message, the flag overriding detection, an unsupported name writing nothing, refusal leaving the file byte-for-byte unchanged, forced replacement of a longer previous file, a piped run completing, a cancelled prompt and a declined one, and the single-file side-effect test proving .gitignore, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are untouched, none of them created when absent, and harnaas.json the only entry that appeared
281	- CLAUDE.md records the two load-bearing decisions — refuse before asking, and a decline is not a cancellation — and .golangci.yaml's wrapcheck exemptions are now precise per-package signatures covering paths.ProjectRoot, manifest.Path and harness.Lookup, each of which returns a finished user-facing diagnostic
282	
283	**Learnings:**
284	- Under `go test`, interactive.CanPrompt short-circuits to "no" at the testing.Testing() gate before the stream test, so "a piped run does not prompt" can only be asserted in-process as "init completes and writes without blocking". Reaching the prompt paths at all needs HARNAAS_TEST_TTY=1 to force the gate on plus ACCESSIBLE=1 so huh runs synchronously against a strings.Reader — which is what makes the decline ("n\n" on stdin) and cancel (a pre-cancelled context) cases testable without a terminal.
285	- t.Setenv forbids t.Parallel, so the four prompt-gate tests are the only serial ones in init_test.go. That is the practical cost of the environment-driven gates, and it is contained by keeping every other init test driven purely through the command's own streams and an explicitly-passed project root.
286	- wrapcheck's extra-ignore-sigs is matched as a substring of the signature it prints, so `harness.Lookup(` and `manifest.Path(` are valid entries and are far more precise than the leading-dot form (`.Lookup(`) the existing config used — worth preferring, since `.Lookup(` would silently exempt any future Lookup in any package.
287	- testifylint's encoded-compare fires on any assert.Equal whose expected string parses as JSON, including a "this file is byte-for-byte unchanged" assertion over a manifest fixture. Splitting both sides on newlines satisfies it and keeps the assertion stronger than JSONEq, which would pass on a file init had silently reformatted.
288	- cobra renders a help group's header at the position its first command was attached, so the commented-out install and lint attachments had to move below the real init attachment for the eventual order to match helpGroups. Ungrouped commands (cobra's generated `help`) land under an "Additional Commands:" heading, which is why the root's help now shows two sections.
289	- Section 8's tasks divide cleanly into work that could not be split further: the command has no useful intermediate state between "flags parsed" and "file written", since a constructor attached to the root with a RunE that scaffolds nothing would be a shipped command that does nothing. Sections 9 (guardrail tests) and 10 (verification) are all that remain, and 9.1–9.4 are largely satisfied already by tests written alongside sections 3, 4 and 8 — the outstanding pieces are the forbidigo AST test (9.3), the per-user-directory redirect harness (9.5) and the tagged end-to-end binary test (9.6).
290

# gnhf run: opsx-apply-acf923

Objective: see .gnhf/runs/opsx-apply-acf923/prompt.md

## Iteration Log

### Iteration 1

**Summary:** Completed Section 1 of the add-harnaas-foundation OpenSpec change, scaffolding the harnaas Go repository and its full toolchain (9/74 tasks), with build, lint, format and goreleaser checks all passing.

**Changes:**
- Go module github.com/harnaas/harnaas at Go 1.26.5 with the cmd/harnaas, cmd/harnaas/cli and internal/ layout; cmd/harnaas/main.go is a deliberate buildable placeholder that section 2's entrypoint work replaces
- mise as the single toolchain and task entry point: mise.toml pins Go 1.26.5 and golangci-lint 2.11.3 with gotestsum as a postinstall step, and mise-tasks/ provides build, fmt, test, a sequential check task, and lint fanning out to lint:go, lint:gofmt, lint:gomod, lint:mise, lint:shellcheck and lint:licenses
- .golangci.yaml on the v2 schema with the standard set plus ~60 extended linters, integration/e2e build tags, strict nolintlint, and forbidigo rules banning os.Getwd (naming paths.ProjectRoot(ctx)) and cobra's Print* helpers (naming cmd.OutOrStdout())
- .goreleaser.yaml building cmd/harnaas for darwin/linux/windows on amd64/arm64 with CGO disabled, stamping Version and Commit into cmd/harnaas/cli/versioninfo via ldflags
- .github/workflows/ci.yml with SHA-pinned actions and lint, licenses, test and test-windows jobs behind a single 'ci' aggregator job intended as the required status check
- .allowed-licenses SPDX allowlist plus a go-licenses gate wired as the lint:licenses task
- CLAUDE.md recording the imported architecture rules (flat cli package, no persistent flags, entrypoint-owns-errors, exit-code taxonomy, signal re-raise, context-carried project root, strict-vs-lenient decoding, logging privacy, atomic writes) with AGENTS.md pointing at it

**Learnings:**
- The reference entire.io CLI is checked out at C:\Users\brasp\Documents\GitHub\cli and its mise.toml, .golangci.yaml, mise-tasks/lint/* and .github/workflows are directly adaptable — future iterations should read from it rather than inventing conventions.
- A GitHub Actions aggregator job can only 'needs' jobs within its own workflow file, so task 1.7's 'workflows for test and lint plus a single aggregator job' was implemented as one ci.yml containing all jobs.
- Task 1.1 asks for directories that git cannot track empty; cmd/harnaas needs a buildable main.go (placeholder here, replaced by task 2.2) and internal/ was given a README recording the import-cycle-only extraction rule.
- mise on Windows requires 'mise trust' before any task runs, and it happily executes the /bin/sh mise-tasks scripts via git-bash — but the CI windows job deliberately uses plain 'go test ./...' instead.
- mise-tasks/lint/gomod fails on a brand-new repo because 'git status --porcelain go.mod' reports the untracked file; it only passes once go.mod is committed.
- Verification tooling not installed locally can be run one-off via 'mise x <tool> -- <cmd>' — used for 'goreleaser check' and yq to validate .goreleaser.yaml and ci.yml without adding them to mise.toml.

### Iteration 2

**Summary:** Completed Section 2 of the add-harnaas-foundation change — the process entrypoint, two-stage signal handling, error-rendering contract and exit-code taxonomy — plus the versioninfo package it depends on, taking the change from 9/74 to 17/74 tasks with lint, format and tests all clean.

**Changes:**
- internal/procsignal records the signal that initiated shutdown in an atomic.Value, giving the entrypoint a single source of truth for whether a context.Canceled was signal-driven and by which signal, so SIGTERM exits 143 rather than impersonating an interrupt's 130
- cmd/harnaas/cli/versioninfo exposes ldflags-stamped Version/Commit with a pure resolve core: an explicit stamp beats Go's embedded build info, which beats the dev placeholder; goreleaser's existing -X stamps now target a package that exists
- cmd/harnaas/cli/errors.go adds AlreadyPrintedError with Unwrap and the NewAlreadyPrintedError constructor, so a command that printed a friendly explanation can suppress the entrypoint's restatement without hiding the cause from errors.Is/errors.As
- cmd/harnaas/cli/root.go builds the root command with cobra's error and usage printing silenced, no persistent flags, a version template carrying the commit, and Args: cobra.NoArgs so an unrecognized verb is reported as an unknown command even before subcommands exist
- cmd/harnaas/main.go replaces the placeholder with the full process contract: versioninfo.Load, a cancellable root context, a two-stage signal handler (first cancels and prints the force-quit notice, second forces exit), dieFromSignal re-raising the original signal with a 128+signum fallback, and the error switch routing already-printed / unknown-command-or-flag / positional-arg / plain errors
- The exit-code taxonomy is stated as documented constants in main.go — 0 success, 1 runtime failure, 2 reserved for lint findings with the negative rule that no other command may return it — and a test asserts no entrypoint error path can produce 2
- Test coverage for section 2: a re-executed-child test proving the process is killed by the signal rather than exiting normally (skipped on Windows), the 128+signum mapping including a non-numeric signal, terminatingSignal's gate on a recorded signal, every branch of the error switch driven by both synthetic and real cobra errors, and proof cobra prints neither error nor usage itself
- cobra v1.10.2 and testify v1.11.1 added to go.mod, with the go-licenses gate confirming every new transitive dependency's license is on the allowlist

**Learnings:**
- Task ordering in tasks.md is not a strict dependency order: task 2.2 ("load version info") requires task 4.1's versioninfo package and a root command from section 3, so 4.1 was pulled forward. Section 3.1 was left unchecked deliberately — the root command exists but has no help groups or subcommand attachments yet.
- Cobra's legacyArgs makes a root command with no subcommands accept arbitrary positional args, so `harnaas bogus` silently printed help and exited 0. Setting `Args: cobra.NoArgs` on the root produces cobra's own `unknown command "bogus" for "harnaas"` message, which the entrypoint's classifier already matches, and stays correct once subcommands land.
- mise tasks cannot be launched from the PowerShell tool on this machine ("program not found" — mise shells out to `sh`); they must be run through the Bash tool. Running golangci-lint directly via `mise x -- golangci-lint run` is the way to see lint results, because a failing sibling task in the `lint` fan-out kills the whole group before lint:go reports.
- The `testifylint` linter with enable-all requires `require.*` rather than `assert.*` for every error assertion (ErrorIs/ErrorAs), which is the only lint class the new code tripped.
- `go get` alone leaves go.sum incomplete for test-only transitive deps (davecgh/go-spew via testify); `go mod tidy` is required before the packages will even build.

### Iteration 3

**Summary:** Completed Section 3 of the add-harnaas-foundation change — help groups, the explicit-attachment rule, the local --json flag helper and the stdout/stderr output contract — taking the change from 17/74 to 22/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.

**Changes:**
- cmd/harnaas/cli/root.go declares the root's help groups (setup, then assets) in display order, and adds addCommand(parent, child, groupID) as the single way a command joins the tree: it declares the group on first use, sets the child's GroupID, and panics naming command and group on an unknown id — surfacing a wiring typo at construction instead of cobra's execute-time panic
- NewRootCmd now carries the commented-out constructor calls for init/install/lint in helpGroups order, making the function the whole readable command tree and documenting where each future command attaches
- cmd/harnaas/cli/flags.go adds addJSONFlag registering --json locally on a command, and jsonRequested reading it back with an undeclared flag answering 'not requested' rather than panicking, so shared rendering helpers can ask unconditionally
- cmd/harnaas/cli/output.go states the output contract in one place and implements it: printJSON writes the document to cmd.OutOrStdout() indented, with HTML escaping off so an ampersand in a source ref survives verbatim, and newline-terminated; advisef sends progress and warning text to cmd.ErrOrStderr()
- cmd/harnaas/cli/root_test.go covers section 3.5 and 3.2: the root declares no persistent flags and a subcommand inherits nothing; --json is accepted only on the command that declares it and fails as 'unknown flag: --json' on a sibling and on the root; groups are declared in display order and none is declared empty; addCommand rejects an unknown group; and an AST pass over non-test sources asserts the package declares no init, so the no-self-registration rule survives a gochecknoinits suppression
- cmd/harnaas/cli/output_test.go proves stdout carries a single parseable JSON document while advisef output lands on stderr, that the ampersand is not rewritten to its HTML escape, that the document ends in exactly one newline, and that an unencodable value returns an error rather than truncating stdout
- Tasks 3.1 through 3.5 checked off in openspec/changes/add-harnaas-foundation/tasks.md

**Learnings:**
- Cobra renders a help header for every declared group whether or not it has members — verified with a scratch test showing a bare 'Empty Commands:' line. That is why helpGroups is a declaration list and addCommand declares a group only on first use: eager declaration would show empty headings for install and lint until their own changes land. The cost is that group display order equals command attachment order, which TestHelpGroupsAreDeclaredInDisplayOrder pins.
- Cobra's checkCommandGroups panics at execute time for a command whose GroupID names an undeclared group, but AddCommand itself does no checking — so a group declared after the commands that use it is a latent panic, not a compile error.
- Section 3.5's 'wrong positional-argument count prints the subcommand's usage' and 'an unrecognized subcommand exits non-zero' were already covered by iteration 2's main_test.go (TestReportErrorShowsTheDeepestSubcommandUsageForAnArgCountError and TestErrorSwitchClassifiesRealCobraErrors); only the persistent-flag and unknown---json assertions were still missing.
- With no subcommands attached, cobra's --help block is skipped entirely (HasAvailableSubCommands is false), so declaring groups on today's root would have been invisible anyway — the empty-header problem only appears once init lands.
- golangci-lint's `unused` counts usage from _test.go files, so addJSONFlag, jsonRequested, printJSON, advisef and addCommand stay lint-clean while no command uses them yet.
- parser.ParseDir is deprecated and would trip staticcheck SA1019; the AST guardrail test uses os.ReadDir plus parser.ParseFile with parser.SkipObjectResolution instead — worth reusing for task 9.3's forbidigo AST test.
- Asserting 'the HTML escape is absent' needs the escape written as a Go interpreted string ("\\u0026"), not a raw-string literal — a raw string containing the bare character makes the assertion trivially fail against its own input.

### Iteration 4

**Summary:** Added the paths and logging foundation packages (tasks 4.2 and 4.3) and wired both into the entrypoint, taking the add-harnaas-foundation change from 22/74 to 24/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.

**Changes:**
- cmd/harnaas/cli/paths resolves the project root by walking up for a .git marker — accepting the file form git writes in a worktree or submodule, and letting the nearest enclosing repository win as git itself does — through a pure Resolve(startDir) that takes a directory rather than reading one
- paths.WithDiscoveredRoot is the single sanctioned reader of the process working directory, carrying the resolved root or the failure in the context; the forbidigo suppression lives there, inside the abstraction the ban's message names
- paths.ProjectRoot(ctx) surfaces the discovery failure at the moment a command asks for a root, so --version, --help and an unknown-command diagnostic keep working outside a repository; a context that never established a root reports ErrRootNotEstablished as a wiring failure distinct from the user-facing *NoProjectRootError
- *NoProjectRootError is typed so a command can recognise the condition without matching message text, and renders as problem-then-fix: which directory was searched, then to run harnaas inside a repository or create one with git init
- cmd/harnaas/cli/logging writes structured slog records to a file under the user's cache directory (HARNAAS_LOG_FILE overrides it, HARNAAS_LOG_LEVEL sets the threshold, both documented at their only read site), never to a terminal stream
- logging discards records where the log file cannot be opened, rather than the reference CLI's fallback to stderr, and Open returns no error because there is nowhere to report one to — a warning on the terminal is the interleaving the log file exists to prevent
- logging.WithCommand and logging.WithComponent label every record with the command the user ran and the subsystem that produced it, ahead of the call site's own attributes; the API takes slog.Attr only, so every logged value arrives as a named field
- The package doc states the privacy rule as a hard rule with harnaas's own reason: the files it handles are a team's instructions and rules, exactly the content nobody expects to find copied into a log they did not know existed
- main.go establishes the project root and opens the log before executing the command tree, and records the run's outcome by exit code and error *type* — never the error message, because errors from later phases will quote the manifest that produced them
- Test coverage: resolution from a nested directory matching resolution from the root, the marker-file form, the nearest-repository rule, the outside-a-repository diagnostic naming directory and fix, context carrying and key isolation, plus logging tests that redirect stdout, stderr and slog's default logger and assert on cleanup that nothing reached any of them

**Learnings:**
- Logging cannot live under the project: task 8.11 requires that after init no .harnaas/ directory exists and harnaas.json is the only file that appeared, so the log file must go under os.UserCacheDir. Task 9.5's 'redirect home, cache and config under t.TempDir' harness confirms per-user state is where harnaas keeps everything that is not the manifest.

The uninitialised logger must also be a discarding logger rather than slog.Default(), which writes to stderr — a stray log call before Open would otherwise print.

- printJSON in cmd/harnaas/cli/output.go now encodes through jsonutil.Marshal and writes the finished bytes, so the --json document and the manifest init will write share one definition of the format, and an unencodable value returns an error with stdout still empty instead of a half-streamed document ahead of the entrypoint's error message

**Learnings:**
- golangci-lint's std-error-handling exclusion preset already covers os.Remove and *.Close, so `_ = os.Remove(...)` and a deferred Close stay clean even with errcheck's check-blank: true — but Sync is not on that list, so the best-effort directory flush still needs an explicit nolint with a reason. This is the boundary that decides which dropped errors need a suppression and which do not.
- testifylint's encoded-compare rule rejects asserting an exact JSON string with assert.Equal and pushes toward assert.JSONEq, which would defeat a test whose whole subject is indentation and trailing newline. Splitting the document on newlines and comparing the resulting []string satisfies the linter and reads better, because a failure names the line that moved.
- Injecting a mid-write failure portably needs a seam: making the rename fail is platform-specific (POSIX rename over a regular file succeeds), so passing the flush step as a function parameter to an unexported implementation is the way to exercise the failure path on both Windows and POSIX. Unlike a package-level var it does not force the test to give up t.Parallel.
- On Windows the staging file must be closed before the deferred os.Remove can delete it, so the write/flush/close sequence has to close on every path including the ones where write or flush failed — otherwise the 'no staging file survives' guarantee holds on POSIX and silently fails on Windows.

- uiform.Confirm returns ErrCancelled for a dismissed prompt rather than folding cancellation into a 'no', because the init spec requires a cancelled prompt to write nothing and exit non-zero while a decline is an ordinary answer

- Test coverage: a table over every prompting gate including piped streams and the CI=false escape hatch, each agent sentinel individually, real os.Pipe and bytes.Buffer both answering 'not a terminal', the styling gates, accessible mode completing a prompt against non-terminal streams, cancellation reported separately from declining, and the theme's unstyled-titles and accent-selection guarantees
- charm.land/huh/v2, charm.land/lipgloss/v2 and golang.org/x/term added to go.mod, with the go-licenses gate confirming all 20 new transitive dependencies are on the allowlist
- CLAUDE.md's non-interactive completeness section now records the two load-bearing decisions — prompting resolved from streams rather than a controlling terminal, and a cancelled prompt distinct from a 'no' — so a later change does not reintroduce either
- Tasks 4.5 and 4.7 checked off in openspec/changes/add-harnaas-foundation/tasks.md, completing Section 4

**Learnings:**
- huh v2 reports a cancelled context as huh.ErrTimeout, not ErrUserAborted or context.Canceled — its run() maps tea.ErrProgramKilled to ErrTimeout because a timeout is the only reason it cancels a context itself. Matching on huh's error alone silently misclassifies a signal-driven cancellation; consulting ctx.Err() is the only reliable test.
- huh's accessible path (runAccessible) ignores the context entirely and runs synchronously against the given reader/writer, so a cancellation arriving mid-question is invisible until the prompt returns. Any wrapper that must honour cancellation has to check the context after the run as well as before it.
- Accessible mode is what makes a prompt testable at all: the full-screen path needs a terminal to redraw, while runAccessible works against a strings.Reader and a bytes.Buffer. A test that sets ACCESSIBLE and completes a prompt on non-terminal streams is therefore a genuine assertion that accessible mode was honoured, not a proxy for one.
- huh's accessible PromptString breaks out of its re-prompt loop on EOF rather than looping forever, and an empty line falls through to the default — so a test can feed a bare reader without hanging.
- The reference CLI's /dev/tty probe plus raw-mode ioctl is POSIX-only and would need three build-tagged files that do nothing on Windows. Testing the command's own streams for terminal-ness covers the same cases portably and additionally catches redirection, which the /dev/tty probe misses.
- lint:gomod necessarily fails in any iteration that adds a dependency, because it runs `go mod tidy` and then asserts `git status --porcelain go.mod go.sum` is empty — uncommitted additions are indistinguishable from an untidy tree. The signal to check is that `go mod tidy` produced no *further* change beyond the intended one.
- golangci-lint accepted the whole huh/lipgloss surface without a single suppression beyond the two gosec G115 fd conversions, so the charm v2 stack imposes no lint debt on this configuration.

### Iteration 8

**Summary:** Added the manifest document, strict decoding and root-only discovery package (Section 6, tasks 6.1–6.8), taking the add-harnaas-foundation change from 32/74 to 40/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.

**Changes:**
- cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest declares the decoded document — integer version, harnesses, sources map and an assets array whose entries keep their array index and their written form — with every field uninterpreted: an empty field means 'not declared', never 'declared as the default', which is the distinction the interpretation layer needs to default targets and scope
- Version is read on its own, leniently, ahead of the strict pass, so a manifest written by a newer harnaas is refused with an upgrade message instead of a complaint about the first field this binary happens not to know; reading it with json.Unmarshal rather than a streaming decoder also rejects trailing data that would otherwise be dropped in silence
- Strict decoding rejects unknown fields at both the document and asset-object level, malformed JSON with a file:line:column naming the parse position, and wrongly shaped fields named in the author's vocabulary rather than Go's — via a field-to-shape table, because reflection would print []string and map[string]string at a person reading JSON
- Asset entries decode from json.RawMessage with the index in hand, accepting the string and object forms chosen from the first non-space byte and rejecting every other JSON type; encoding/json attaches no array index to its errors and an entry has no other name until its id is inferred
- Every decode failure returns a nil document, so a partially decoded manifest can never reach a later phase and install a subset of what the project declared while reporting success
- manifest.Load resolves the manifest from the context-carried project root, and manifest.Path is the single place the file's location is assembled so init and install cannot disagree about where it is
- The search for a harnaas.json below the root runs before the missing-manifest check and skips dot-directories plus node_modules and vendor: a vendored library's manifest is its own, and a project whose only manifest sits in a subdirectory is never told to run `harnaas init`
- Three diagnostics: *DecodeError carrying location, a one-line problem and an edit; *NotFoundError naming `harnaas init`; and *SubdirectoryError naming the file that will never be read and the one harnaas does read
- Test coverage for section 6.8 plus a table asserting the problem-then-fix shape across all ten failure modes, that no remedy offers a fix command, and an AST guardrail over non-test sources asserting no write call and no jsonutil import has crept into the read-only loader
- CLAUDE.md records the two new load-bearing decisions — the version pre-pass and the root-only rule with its dependency-directory skips — and .golangci.yaml exempts paths.ProjectRoot from wrapcheck, because its error is already a finished user-facing diagnostic that a caller would only prefix with plumbing

**Learnings:**
- json.Unmarshal validates the whole input and rejects a second top-level value, so a version pre-pass over the full document makes an explicit trailing-data check unreachable — the check was written, proved dead, and removed in favour of documenting that the pre-pass settles it.
- encoding/json reports an unknown field as a bare fmt.Errorf, not a typed error, so recognising it means matching the literal prefix `json: unknown field ` and unquoting the rest; the translation falls through to reporting the raw message if that wording ever changes, which is worse but never wrong.
- An asset entry decoded from its own json.RawMessage carries offsets relative to the entry, so any line:column derived from them names the wrong line in the file. Scoping the locator to an entry and having it refuse to report a location at all is the fix — one comment in one place rather than a mutation at each call site.
- wrapcheck fires on errors returned from any other package including same-module ones, which will hit every future command calling paths.ProjectRoot. Configuring extra-ignore-sigs once is the right answer where the callee's error is already a complete problem-then-fix diagnostic; wrapping it would prefix a finished message with the caller's plumbing.
- The `exhaustive` linter's default (default-signifies-exhaustive: false) makes a switch on reflect.Kind a lint failure even with a default clause, which is a practical reason to describe expected JSON shapes from a field-name table rather than by reflection — and the table produces better messages anyway.
- Section 7's interpretation layer is now fully unblocked: it reads Document/AssetEntry, and the two decode-time distinctions it depends on are already pinned by tests — nil vs empty Targets, and empty-string overrides meaning undeclared.

### Iteration 9

**Summary:** Added the manifest interpretation layer's parsing half — source values, the asset string grammar, local containment and type/id inference (Section 7, tasks 7.1–7.4) — taking the add-harnaas-foundation change from 40/74 to 44/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.

**Changes:**
- cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest/violation.go adds Violation — an asset index, a field name, a problem and a fix — carrying its location as data rather than only inside its sentence, so the aggregate error section 7.8 builds can order itself identically on every run; it deliberately does not satisfy `error`, because a type that did would invite a caller to return the first violation it saw
- cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest/source.go parses a `sources` value into kind, repository and ref and resolves nothing: no fetch, no stat, so a manifest validates with neither network nor filesystem. The kind switch lists every registered kind so one added to the roster without a case reports itself unrecognized rather than being parsed by whichever branch was last
- A `github` source with no `@ref` is rejected rather than defaulted to a branch — the manifest exists to state which version of somebody else's content the repository trusts, and a default would make two installs of one manifest produce different files; a `local` source pins nothing and must name a directory under `.harnaas`
- cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest/assetref.go implements the asset string grammar, choosing between the keyed remote form and the project-local form by prefix rather than by trying one and falling back, so a string in neither form is reported as what it is instead of as a failed parse of a form its author never used
- Containment is checked textually before anything is opened, because a path that escapes `.harnaas` must never be read — not even to discover whether it exists; absolute paths in both the POSIX and Windows spellings, UNC paths and any backslash are refused on every platform, so a committed manifest cannot name two different files depending on who ran install
- An absolute path gets its own diagnostic rather than the general 'neither form' one, because the fix is to move content into the repository rather than to add a prefix to the same path
- CheckSourceKey is separate from ParseAssetRef because the grammar is a property of the string and the key is a property of the document: the same entry is correct in one manifest and wrong in another, and only the second failure can list the keys that would have worked
- InferType and InferID are separate functions so the object form can suppress inference one field at a time — an entry declaring `type` for an unconventional layout still wants its id inferred, and must not be refused for a directory name nobody is relying on; the id keeps a dotfile leaf whole, since stripping `.editorconfig`'s extension would leave nothing
- Test coverage across both new files: every accepted form, ten rejected `sources` values, eleven rejected asset strings, the last-@ ref split, inference for all five types including a nested source path, and an assertion that a violation renders as problem, blank line, fix with no remedy offering a command that edits the manifest
- CLAUDE.md records the three load-bearing decisions — why decoding and interpretation share a package while differing in when they stop, why a GitHub source is always pinned and paths are checked textually, and why type and id are inferred separately; the manifest package doc is rewritten to describe the two layers rather than to promise a separate one

**Learnings:**
- The interpretation layer does not earn its own package under harnaas's stated extraction rule. `manifest` and a hypothetical `assets` package would both be imported by the same callers (the flat cli package, and add-harnaas-install's adapters), so there is no import cycle to break — the rule says the code belongs in `manifest`. Iteration 8's package doc had promised a separate layer; that promise was the thing to change, not the rule.
- golangci-lint's `errname` rejects a type named `Violation` that has an `Error() string` method, demanding the `XxxError` form. Renaming the method to `String()` is the better fix than renaming the type: a single violation is never what a command returns, so it should not satisfy `error` at all, and the linter's complaint turned out to be pointing at a real design question.
- `unparam` with check-exported fires on an unexported constructor whose field parameter always receives the same value, which will happen to every helper written ahead of the call sites that will vary it. Naming the narrow case (assetSourceViolation) rather than suppressing the linter keeps the diff honest — sections 7.5–7.7 will add the sibling constructors when they add the fields.
- `path.Clean` treats a backslash as an ordinary character, so a keyed path like `acme:skills\review` passes every containment check and produces a ref naming a file that exists on Windows and not on Linux. The grammar has to reject backslashes explicitly, ahead of cleaning; the absolute-path check has to run first so `C:\...` and `\\share\...` get the message about absolute paths instead.
- `path.Ext` treats a leading dot as the whole extension, so stripping unconditionally turns `.editorconfig` into an empty id. Only a non-empty remainder can replace the leaf.
- testifylint's useless-assert rejects `assert.Equal(t, f(), f())`, which is the obvious way to write 'this function returns a stable list'. Comparing both calls against a literal expected slice is what the linter wants and is a stronger assertion anyway, because it pins the order rather than only its stability.
- The Bash tool's working directory persists between calls, so a `cd` into a package directory silently rescopes a later `go test ./...` or `golangci-lint run ./...` to that package — which reports 0 issues and looks like a pass. Prefix repo-wide verification with an explicit cd to the repository root.

- CLAUDE.md records the two load-bearing decisions — a default is inherited and checked once, and a wrong scope is refused rather than degraded — together with why the refusal needs a seam to be testable before the first harness without a per-user location is added

**Learnings:**
- Validating an inherited default per asset would multiply one mistake by the number of entries that inherited it, so the manifest's `harnesses` list is checked once at DocumentIndex and ResolveTargets checks only what the entry itself declared. The consequence is that an inherited unrecognized name still reaches Asset.Targets — which is safe only because a document with any violation is never handed to a later phase, and that is now a load-bearing invariant rather than a convenience.
- Section 7.7's core rule is untestable against the real roster: claude-code is the only entry and it has PerUserLocation true, so there is no target for which `user` scope can be refused. Passing harness.HasPerUserLocation as a parameter to an unexported resolveScope — the same seam pattern jsonutil.writeFileAtomic already uses for its flush step — is what keeps the rule from rotting until the first harness that lacks a per-user location is added.
- A per-field violation helper has to produce a field name that sorts deterministically, which is why an unrecognized target is spelled `assets[3].targets[0]` rather than sharing one `assets[3].targets` field with its siblings. Lexical rather than numeric ordering of the bracketed index is a known and accepted consequence — 7.9 specifies ordering by index then field, and lexical field order is exactly that.
- gocritic's unlambda fires on a test closure that only forwards to the function it wraps, so a seam test wanting to pass the real implementation must pass the function value directly rather than wrapping it for readability; the explanatory comment has to move above the call site.
- Two test files for one source file is already the established convention here (jsonutil splits json_test.go external from write_test.go internal), so an exported-surface test in package manifest_test plus an internal test for the seam needs no justification beyond naming the internal one asset_internal_test.go.

**Changes:**
